# fyne and gtk4 have no error-boundary emitter, and need none: by the time
# passDeclarative flattens their views, every raise under a boundary is
# resolved to its handler (Call.ResolvedHandler) and the handler has had its
# updaters injected, so the boundary holds nothing and is spliced into what it
# holds. Every window's content is under one -- each platform's override of
# ui.window wraps it in the boundary its @error is -- which is what made that
# general. They used to refuse a boundary a program wrote by name, before the
# renderer met it.
#
# The raise is caught where the click runs: the handler is a catch block that
# recovers the payload and runs the boundary's body.

sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=fy boundary.sngl
grep 'recover\(\)' fy/model.go
grep 'm.caught__inst0 = e.Message' fy/model.go
! stderr 'panic'

sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --out=gt boundary.sngl
grep 'recover\(\)' gt/model.go
grep 'm.caught__inst0 = e.Message' gt/model.go

sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=ht boundary.sngl
sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=bt boundary.sngl
sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=an boundary.sngl

-- boundary.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main node {
    var caught = ""
    boundary(@error(e) { caught = e.message }) {
        button #retry(text="Go", @click { error.raise("boom", "") })
    }
    text(value=caught)
}

window {
    main
}
